purpose: Compatibility of provider arbitration models with observed release signatures. A HYPOTHESIS tool: a compatible model is not proven; a model that never reproduces a signature is contradicted only within the explored parameter ranges.

provenance: FACT: send offsets (Playwright request events) and response offsets (CHECKOUT_PRE_POST + network duration) on the dispatch clock
INFERENCE: edge arrival = x-vercel-id embedded number (UNDOCUMENTED meaning) on the dispatch clock
FACT: Slot Watch read request/response offsets, shifted to the dispatch clock
INFERENCE: every one of our requests (7 browsers and the Slot Watch) left from one public IP
FACT: send and response offsets on the runner clock
INFERENCE: edge = send + 20 ms (no provider stamp retained)
Reads are not replayed (they timed out client-side at 5 s that day)
FACT: journal createdAt/updatedAt on the runner network-corrected clock
Reads are not replayed (few samples, PC wall clock)

search.ranges: log-uniform: crowd checkouts 20–400, arrival mean 0.1–8 s, pre-release share 0–0.6, reads 5–60/s, pre-lock work 0.2–1.5 s, in-lock work 0.15–1.5 s (C: 0.3–5 s, D: 0.15–5 s); family knobs as in src/arbitration/release-replay.ts; half of the draws add a replica/cache read path (share 0–0.8) that the fixed grid does not have
